entities.name: Structural transformations and structural order in GST materials drive pronounced optical contrast and tunability; in particular, reversible amorphous–crystalli
entities.description: Structural transformations and structural order in GST materials drive pronounced optical contrast and tunability; in particular, reversible amorphous–crystalline transitions increase the refractive index and extinction coefficient in the crystalline phase and produce measurable reflectance changes across the visible range.
entities.evidence_span: Phase-change Ge–Sb–Te (GST) materials exhibit pronounced optical contrast and tunability driven by structural transformations

evidence_spans: Phase-change Ge–Sb–Te (GST) materials exhibit pronounced optical contrast and tunability driven by structural transformations

GST materials undergo reversible amorphous–crystalline phase transitions during which the refractive index and extinction coefficient increase significantly in the crystalline phase across a broad spectral range.

The sensitivity of optical reflectivity to structural order has been demonstrated in Ge2Sb2Te5 films, where variations in crystalline phase and degree of order result in measurable changes in reflectance across the visible spectral range [20, 21].

entities.name: The authors hypothesize that in as-deposited crystalline GST (GeTe-Sb2Te3 pseudo-binary) films, composition-dependent structure, microstructure, and morphology
entities.description: The authors hypothesize that in as-deposited crystalline GST (GeTe-Sb2Te3 pseudo-binary) films, composition-dependent structure, microstructure, and morphology govern the initial broadband optical response, and that this can be systematically correlated through a composition-resolved study without intermediate phase transitions.
entities.evidence_span: Here, we report a systematic study of composition-resolved opto-structural property relationships in as-deposited crystalline GST films spanning Ge3Sb2Te6, Ge2Sb2Te5, and GeSb2Te4 within a single CVD process, avoiding intermediate phase transitions. This enables direct correlations between composition, microstructure, morphology, and broadband optical response across 400-1700 nm.

evidence_spans: Here, we report a systematic study of composition-resolved opto-structural property relationships in as-deposited crystalline GST films spanning Ge3Sb2Te6, Ge2Sb2Te5, and GeSb2Te4 within a single CVD process, avoiding intermediate phase transitions. This enables direct correlations between composition, microstructure, morphology, and broadband optical response across 400-1700 nm.

We demonstrate that composition-dependent structural and morphological features strongly govern the initial optical behavior, while laser-induced modifications introduce additional opportunity for spatially selective tuning of the optical response.

entities.name: The authors hypothesize that crystalline GST films can function as broadband-tunable, spatially programmable photonic elements, with optical properties controll
entities.description: The authors hypothesize that crystalline GST films can function as broadband-tunable, spatially programmable photonic elements, with optical properties controlled jointly by compositional design and localized laser processing, enabling reconfigurable photonic and adaptive optical applications.
entities.evidence_span: These findings establish crystalline GST films as a platform for broadband-tunable, spatially programmable photonic elements, controllable through both compositional design and localized laser processing.

evidence_spans: These findings establish crystalline GST films as a platform for broadband-tunable, spatially programmable photonic elements, controllable through both compositional design and localized laser processing.

Overall, this work establishes a platform for controlled, spatially programmable tuning of broadband optical properties in GeTe-Sb2Te3 pseudo-binary materials, enabling their application in reconfigurable photonic systems and adaptive optical devices.

We demonstrate that composition-dependent structural and morphological features strongly govern the initial optical behavior, while laser-induced modifications introduce additional opportunity for spatially selective tuning of the optical response.

Here, we report a systematic study of composition-resolved opto-structural property relationships in as-deposited crystalline GST films spanning Ge3Sb2Te6, Ge2Sb2Te5, and GeSb2Te4 within a single CVD process, avoiding intermediate phase transitions. This enables direct correlations between composition, microstructure, morphology, and broadband optical response across 400-1700 nm.

Here, we report a systematic study of composition-resolved opto-structural property relationships in as-deposited crystalline GST films spanning Ge3Sb2Te6, Ge2Sb2Te5, and GeSb2Te4 within a single CVD process, avoiding intermediate phase transitions. This enables direct correlations between composition, microstructure, morphology, and broadband optical response across 400-1700 nm.

These findings establish crystalline GST films as a platform for broadband-tunable, spatially programmable photonic elements, controllable through both compositional design and localized laser processing.

Here, we report a systematic study of composition-resolved opto-structural property relationships in as-deposited crystalline GST films spanning Ge3Sb2Te6, Ge2Sb2Te5, and GeSb2Te4 within a single CVD process, avoiding intermediate phase transitions. This enables direct correlations between composition, microstructure, morphology, and broadband optical response across 400-1700 nm.

These findings establish crystalline GST films as a platform for broadband-tunable, spatially programmable photonic elements, controllable through both compositional design and localized laser processing.
